claims.claim: Note-1 identifies impersonation as the root cause of diff failures, which aligns with the failure details in ticket T-26271.
Note-2's operational rule to switch ApplicationSet to AllAtOnce deletion before deleting child apps should be reflected in ticket T-28511's mitigation.
Note-2's restriction that hydrator pilot repos must not use progressive sync until debounce should be added to ticket T-27949.
Note-1 states that T-27327 is deprioritized to next quarter, which should be updated in ticket T-27327.
RFC-001 sync-impersonation proposes a system-wide impersonation flag, but note-1 indicates it will be per-project, creating a conflict.
PRD progressive sync deletion strategy introduces reverse deletion order, but strategy.md still states deletion stays manual, creating a conflict.

Enabling impersonation globally may cause server-side diff on external clusters to ignore destinationServiceAccounts, requiring broad patch permissions and creating a risk of over-privileged identities.
Using reverse deletion order with progressive sync can lead to infinite delete/recreate loops, as observed in ticket T-28511.

proposals.change: Add root cause: impersonation on diff causes missing permissions for cluster-scoped resources.
proposals.citedLine: the CI diff failures (the missing-permissions one, T-26271) got root-caused on the call: with impersonation on, diff runs as the destination service account which doesn't hold patch on cluster-scoped stuff.

proposals.citedLine: hydrator rollback work (the history & rollback ticket, T-27327) is deprioritized to next quarter. dev pair moves to the progressive sync deletion loop instead. ticket should say so.

proposals.citedLine: hydrator pilot repos must not use progressive sync until there's a debounce. the pilot ticket (T-27949) should carry that restriction so the next team doesn't trip it.
